subject: multi kit, multi fraction PD experiment error

messages.author: 8c05e04cfce80cdf
messages.subject: multi kit, multi fraction PD experiment error
parts:
I recently installed MSstatsTMT and would like to test it on a large dataset. It incorporates 4 TMT 11-plex kits (each with 10 samples and an empty channel), and each was pre-fractionated. I exported the PSM search results from Proteome Discoverer following the raw.pd example. However I am getting the following error. 

Error in aggregate.data.frame(mf[1L], mf[-1L], FUN = FUN, ...) :
  no rows to aggregate  

What could be causing this error? I have attached the annotation table but  cannot legally share the data file. I can provide column names if that will help.

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: multi kit, multi fraction PD experiment error
parts:
This error is because of missing rows in the annotation file. It seems like some channel information is missing in some runs. For example, channel 129N is missing from 078_0004_01C_R_Kit3Fraction5_13AUG20_PLA_HUM_ECL_0012_PA_135MIN_MNM_RS_01.raw (see the following scrrenshot)


Another example, channel 131C is missing from 078_0004_01C_R_Kit2Fraction32_13AUG20_PLA_HUM_ECL_0012_PA_135MIN_MNM_RS_01.raw.

MSstatsTMT requries info for each run and each channel. If the channle is empty sample, you can put "Empty" under Condition and Bioreplicate columns. You can use the following code to check which runs have issue:

library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
MSstatsTMT_annotDB %>% group_by(Run) %>% 
  summarise(n = n_distinct(Channel)) %>% 
  filter(n < 11)

  annotDB,

inputPD,
method = "LogSum",
global_norm = TRUE,
reference_norm = FALSE,
remove_norm_channel = FALSE,
remove_empty_channel = TRUE,
MBimpute = FALSE,
maxQuantileforCensored = NULL
)

Thank you.

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: multi kit, multi fraction PD experiment error
parts:
PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat shouldn't remove any samples. Can you share the updated annotation file?

If your mastermix channel is used for normalization, then you should set the Condition and BioReplicate columns in the annotation file to "Norm" so that MSstatsTMT can recognize the mastermix channels. And then set reference_norm = TRUE in proteinSummarization to perform the normalization between runs based on the mastermix channels.
If you want to remove the PSM with any missing values in a run, you can set rmPSM_withMissing_withinRun = TRUE in PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat.

So as a summary, you can first  set the Condition and BioReplicate columns in the annotation file to "Norm", then run the following code

inputPD <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(
  PSMs,
  annotDB,

which.proteinid = "Master.Protein.Accessions",
  rmPSM_withMissing_withinRun = TRUE
)

quant.pd.msstats <- proteinSummarization(
inputPD,
method = "LogSum",
global_norm = TRUE,
reference_norm = TRUE,

remove_norm_channel = FALSE,
remove_empty_channel = TRUE,
MBimpute = FALSE,
maxQuantileforCensored = NULL
)

messages.subject: Re: multi kit, multi fraction PD experiment error
parts:
The annotation file shows channel 126 is the MasterMix sample. But in the example PSM file you shared, all the values in channel 126 is NA. I guess this happens throughout the whole data. PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat function of MSstatsTMT 1.6.3 removes the NA values from the output so you didn't see condition MasterMix. 

MSstatsTMT currently relies on the reference channel (reference_norm method) to perform the normalization between runs, which removes most of the batch effects. I would recommend to use the mastermix for normalization and check whether the samples are clustered together to validate the normalization.
